newsitem.title: USA: Bethlehem to sell BethForge and CENTEC units.
newsitem.headline: Bethlehem to sell BethForge and CENTEC units.

text.p: Bethlehem Steel Corp said Friday it will sell its BethForge and CENTEC businesses in Bethlehem, Pa., to two companies of the West Homestead Engineering and Machinery Co group for an undisclosed price.
The steel maker said it expected to close the sale once the United Steelworkers of America and the buyers signed a new labor agreement.
Bethlehem said Lehigh Forge Corp will buy forging company BethForge and CR Acquisition will buy CENTEC, a supplier of cast iron rolls.
The sale is part of a restructruring plan the company announced in October last year.

Bethlehem took a $370 million after-tax charge in the fourth quarter of 1996 to pay for the restructuring, which also included closing its Bethelehem Structural Products Corp's Structural Mill in the first quarter and trying to sell BethShip Inc's Sparrows Point Yard.
Bethlehem said Friday it ended discussions with Baltimore Shipbuilding and Drydock LLC about the Maryland yard's sale and it would close the yard and sell its assets.
The yard employs about 100 people, while CENTEC has 125 employees and BethForge 450.
The company said CENTEC's buyer CR Acquisition will have a technical relationship with Forcast International of France.
Bethlehem also said BethForge's buyer Lehigh Forge will buy steel from its Pennsylvania Steel Technologies unit in Steelton, Pa.
A company spokeswoman was not immediately available to comment on possible job cuts at the three units.
